subject: Throughput cliff: rapid triage, product mitigations & customer update
messages:
From: Kelly Morris <kelly@clearcart.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jan 2028 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Checkout throughput collapse — losing orders

Hi team,

We saw a sudden drop in checkout throughput starting ~07:40 UTC. Successful checkout rate fell from ~1200/min to ~75/min. The majority of requests are timing out at our side and we have a growing queue. Attaching a short trace (clearcart-request-trace.har) and a slice of logs — you can see repeated 503s and elevated tail latency from your Gen API (tokenization stage appears noisy).

Can someone confirm whether this is an ongoing infra problem on your side or if we should throttle from our end? This is causing real customer impact — paging our ops now.

Thanks,
Kelly Morris
Head of Platform Reliability
ClearCart

Attachments: clearcart-request-trace.har (har), customer-checkout-logs-30jan.txt (log stub)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jan 2028 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Checkout throughput collapse — losing orders

Thanks Kelly — seeing this in our monitoring as well (spike in queue length + p95/p99 jump). Ben, can you confirm if any autoscaler churn or one-off kernel throttling happened at 07:35–07:50 UTC in us-west-2?

Product — Marissa, is there a quick config we can toggle (batch window, kv-cache TTL) that reduces tail amplification without changing model weights? Customer is reporting lost orders.

Evelyn — I'll coordinate comms to ClearCart if we have a short mitigation. Grace, can CS surface contract/slack with their account team so we can loop them in?

Plan I propose: 1) SRE triage immediately, 2) if we confirm a runtime regression, switch ClearCart to a fallback model variant with higher concurrency, 3) customer note within 60 minutes.

Jonas Weber
Director, Product Ops — Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jan 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Checkout throughput collapse — losing orders

Jonas — initial findings: around 07:36 UTC we observed a coordinated increase in tail tokenization latency for the gptx-medium-v2 family on a subset of pods. Autoscaler responded by shedding a few lower-priority instances which created intermittent queueing. I don't see any node crashes or disk pressure. Kernel scheduling metrics show a pattern consistent with per-request jitter (KV cache misses spiking).

Immediate mitigations we tested in staging: 1) reduce dynamic batch window to 5ms — drops p99 by ~120ms but reduces throughput slightly, 2) force-use quantized variant (gptx-qv2-compat) which uses smaller memory working set and sustains concurrency.

Action we recommend for ClearCart now: 1) flip routing to gptx-qv2-compat for their API key (non-disruptive, same surface), 2) temporarily tighten batch window to prioritize latency. I'll open a rollout with rollback guard.

I'll attach the server logs slice (server-logs-20280130.txt) to the internal ticket.

Ben Carter
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference

Attachments: server-logs-20280130.txt (log slice)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jan 2028 12:45:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Checkout throughput collapse — losing orders

Agree with Ben's plan. A couple product notes / checks before we route:
- gptx-qv2-compat has slightly reduced per-token quality on abstractive prompts — we should confirm ClearCart's critical paths (checkout confirmations) are tolerant.
- We can add a brief inference header (X-Model-Variant) so ClearCart can metric-slice and we can track any quality regressions.

Grace — ask CS to pull a representative prompt set (5–10 examples) from ClearCart, so we can smoke-check outputs within 30 minutes post-switch. If outputs degrade meaningfully we'll have an immediate rollback.

I'll draft the customer-facing note once Ben confirms we can flip routing.

Marissa Cole
Head of Product — Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Kelly Morris <kelly@clearcart.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jan 2028 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Checkout throughput collapse — losing orders

Kelly — quick update from the team: we have identified elevated KV-cache miss activity in the gen runtime that caused autoscaler churn and the observed throughput drop. Ben will flip ClearCart's traffic to a compatible quantized variant (no API change) and tighten the batch window to reduce tail latency. We expect this to restore normal throughput within ~20 minutes and will monitor closely.

What we will do now:
- Route your production API key to gptx-qv2-compat (non-breaking).
- Add X-Model-Variant response header so you can filter metrics.
- CS will run 10 representative prompts post-change and report any quality concerns within 30 minutes.

We will send a short incident summary once stabilized. Do you want us to put a one-hour status update in your Slack channel?

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Product Ops — Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 31 Jan 2028 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Post-incident summary & short-term roadmap asks

Summary (what happened): 2028-01-30 07:36 UTC — transient increase in KV cache misses for gptx-medium-v2 family on a set of us-west-2 pods. Autoscaler shed capacity in response to perceived saturation which amplified queueing and produced a throughput cliff for select API keys.

Mitigation applied: We routed ClearCart to gptx-qv2-compat and tightened the batch window. Throughput recovered to baseline within ~18 minutes; no data loss. CS validated a 10-example smoke test; no customer-visible regressions reported.

Short-term asks / roadmap items (product + infra):
- Product: add a per-key model-variant flag in the Console to allow on-the-fly routing for customers with strict SLAs.
- Infra: implement a KV-cache warm-up probe during autoscaler events to avoid cache-thrash amplification.
- Product/Infra: expose X-Model-Variant to customers and add doc blurb on behavior and compatibility tradeoffs.

I'll open engineering tickets for the infra items (SRE-1209) and product feature (PROD-598) and link them to CLR-4721. Recommend a follow-up cross-functional retro Friday to scope next steps.

Ben Carter
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference
